archetypes.name: ci-workflow
archetypes.rationale: The diff replaces zhupanov/agent-lint@v2.3.2 GitHub Action with a manual binary download and direct invocation; the action may provide environment or GITHUB_TOKEN context that the bare invocation silently omits, and --retry-all-errors on curl retries HTTP 4xx responses which could mask a missing release asset.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` around the replacement of the `zhupanov/agent-lint@v2.3.2` Action (which accepted `github-token` and `pedantic: true`) with a manual musl binary download followed by `agent-lint --pedantic .`. Determine whether the Action sets up any working-directory, PATH, GITHUB_TOKEN injection, or token-authenticated API behavior that the manual invocation does not replicate. Check whether `--retry-all-errors` is appropriate for versioned release-asset URLs — this flag retries HTTP 4xx responses such as 404, meaning a permanently missing or renamed asset URL would retry three times and burn minutes rather than failing immediately. Evaluate whether moving gitleaks `sha256sum` integrity verification inside the install conditional means cache hits bypass the integrity check, and assess whether that posture is acceptable given gitleaks is a security scanner. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: prune-nit-design
archetypes.rationale: The new prune-nit-findings feature has a stale header comment in plan-review-loop.sh, a misleading INSCOPE_REMAINING=0 in the disabled path, a Python temp file written adjacent to the findings file rather than to /tmp, and a retained --prune-round-num argv path in plan-review-loop.sh that no caller now passes.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the internal design consistency of the prune-nit-findings implementation across `skills/review/scripts/prune-nit-findings.sh`, `skills/review/scripts/review-core.sh`, and `skills/design/scripts/plan-review-loop.sh`. Specifically check: (1) The Python helper is written to `$FINDINGS_FILE.prune-nit-inline.py` — assess what happens when the findings-file directory is not writable (the outer `set -euo pipefail` means the cat would abort the script non-zero before `set +e` around python3); consider whether using a directory derived from TMPDIR or mktemp would be safer. (2) The `LARCH_PRUNE_NITS_DISABLED` early-exit path emits `INSCOPE_REMAINING=0` regardless of actual in-scope count — check whether this misleads any current or likely future caller. (3) The `plan-review-loop.sh` header comment still says 'this script does not read or write review-round-count.txt' but the new argv-fallback block reads it — verify whether this stale comment is the only documentation gap or whether the `.md` sibling also needs updating. (4) The `--prune-round-num` argv is still accepted and parsed in `plan-review-loop.sh` but `run-step3-review.sh` no longer passes it — confirm whether this is an intentional escape hatch with callers outside the diff or dead code. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
